Yamatai.name: Himiko
Yamatai.note: Known from the Chinese Records of the Three Kingdoms; the location of Yamatai is disputed.
Yamatai.note_zh: 见于中国史书《三国志》，邪马台国的位置至今有争议。

people.name: Himiko
people.known_for: Shaman queen of Yamatai who sent envoys to the Wei court in 239 and received the title Queen of Wa Friendly to Wei.
people.known_for_zh: 邪马台国女王，以巫术治国，239年遣使曹魏，受封“亲魏倭王”。

Yamato.name: Emperor Ōjin
Yamato.note: Traditional dates; historians place him in the late 4th century.
Yamato.note_zh: 传统纪年，史学界一般认为他生活在4世纪后期。

Yamato.name: Emperor Nintoku
Yamato.note: Traditional dates; the largest keyhole mound at Sakai is attributed to him.
Yamato.note_zh: 传统纪年，堺市最大的前方后圆坟被认为是他的陵墓。

Yamato.name: Emperor Yūryaku
Yamato.note: Identified with King Bu of Wa, who sent a letter to the Liu Song court in 478.
Yamato.note_zh: 一般认为即《宋书》中478年上表的倭王武。

Yamato.name: Emperor Kinmei
Yamato.note: Buddhism reached the court from Baekje in his reign.
Yamato.note_zh: 在位期间佛教从百济传入日本朝廷。

Yamato.name: Emperor Sushun
Yamato.note: Killed on the orders of Soga no Umako.

people.name: Emperor Yūryaku
people.known_for: Yamato king identified with King Bu of Wa, who extended royal power and sent a famous letter to the Chinese court.
people.known_for_zh: 大和政权的君主，一般认为即倭王武，扩张王权并向南朝宋上表。

people.name: Emperor Keitai
people.known_for: Ruler from the Echizen region who founded the line from which all later emperors descend, and put down the Iwai Rebellion.
people.known_for_zh: 出身越前地区的君主，开创了后世天皇一脉相承的皇统，平定了磐井之乱。

people.name: Emperor Kinmei
people.known_for: Emperor in whose reign King Seong of Baekje sent a Buddha image and sutras, bringing Buddhism to the Yamato court.
people.known_for_zh: 在位期间百济圣王送来佛像和佛经，佛教由此正式传入大和朝廷。

people.name: Soga no Iname
people.known_for: Great minister who backed the new Buddhist faith and made the Soga clan the most powerful family at court.
people.known_for_zh: 大臣，支持接受新传入的佛教，使苏我氏成为朝廷中最有权势的氏族。

people.name: Mononobe no Moriya
people.known_for: Head of the Mononobe clan who opposed Buddhism and was killed in battle by the Soga and Prince Shōtoku in 587.
people.known_for_zh: 物部氏首领，反对崇佛，587年在与苏我氏和圣德太子的战斗中被杀。

Yamato.name: Empress Suiko
Yamato.note: First reigning empress; Prince Shōtoku served as regent.
Yamato.note_zh: 第一位女天皇，由圣德太子摄政。

Yamato.name: Emperor Kōtoku
Yamato.note: The Taika Reform began in his reign.
Yamato.note_zh: 在位期间开始大化改新。

Yamato.name: Emperor Kōbun
Yamato.note: Defeated by his uncle in the Jinshin War.
Yamato.note_zh: 在壬申之乱中败于叔父大海人皇子。

Yamato.name: Emperor Monmu
Yamato.note: The Taihō Code was issued in 701.

Yamato.name: Empress Genmei
Yamato.note: Moved the capital to Heijō-kyō in 710.

people.name: Prince Shōtoku
people.known_for: Regent for Empress Suiko who promoted Buddhism, issued the Seventeen-Article Constitution and sent envoys to Sui China.
people.known_for_zh: 推古天皇的摄政，弘扬佛教，制定《十七条宪法》，并派遣遣隋使。

people.name: Soga no Umako
people.known_for: Powerful minister who defeated the Mononobe, had Emperor Sushun killed and built Asukadera, Japan's first great temple.
people.known_for_zh: 权臣，击败物部氏，派人刺杀崇峻天皇，并兴建日本第一座大寺飞鸟寺。

people.name: Empress Suiko
people.known_for: First reigning empress of Japan, under whom Buddhism became the faith of the court.
people.known_for_zh: 日本第一位女天皇，在她治下佛教成为朝廷信奉的宗教。

people.name: Ono no Imoko
people.known_for: Envoy who led the mission to Sui China in 607, carrying the letter from the 'Son of Heaven where the sun rises'.
people.known_for_zh: 607年出使隋朝的遣隋使，带去了“日出处天子”的国书。

people.name: Emperor Tenji
people.known_for: As Prince Naka no Ōe he overthrew the Soga in 645 and led the Taika Reform; he later ruled as emperor from Ōtsu.
people.known_for_zh: 即中大兄皇子，645年消灭苏我氏，主导大化改新，后在近江大津即位为天皇。

people.name: Fujiwara no Kamatari
people.known_for: Ally of Prince Naka no Ōe in the coup of 645 and founder of the Fujiwara clan.
people.known_for_zh: 与中大兄皇子共同发动乙巳之变，是藤原氏的始祖。

people.name: Emperor Tenmu
people.known_for: Won the throne in the Jinshin War of 672, strengthened the emperor's power and ordered the first national histories.
people.known_for_zh: 在672年的壬申之乱中夺得皇位，加强天皇权力，下令编纂国史。

people.name: Empress Jitō
people.known_for: Widow of Tenmu who completed his reforms and built Fujiwara-kyō, the first capital laid out on a Chinese grid.
people.known_for_zh: 天武天皇的皇后，继承其改革，营建了第一座仿中国棋盘式布局的都城藤原京。

people.name: Fujiwara no Fuhito
people.known_for: Son of Kamatari who helped draft the Taihō Code of 701 and made the Fujiwara the leading court family.
people.known_for_zh: 藤原镰足之子，参与制定701年的《大宝律令》，使藤原氏成为朝廷第一大族。

people.name: Kakinomoto no Hitomaro
people.known_for: Court poet of the Man'yōshū, later honoured as one of the saints of Japanese poetry.
people.known_for_zh: 《万叶集》的宫廷歌人，后世被尊为“歌圣”。

people.name: Princess Nukata
people.known_for: Leading woman poet of the early Man'yōshū, loved by both Tenji and Tenmu.
people.known_for_zh: 《万叶集》前期的代表女歌人，与天智、天武两位天皇都有情缘。

people.name: Dōshō
people.known_for: Monk who studied under Xuanzang in Chang'an and brought the Hossō school to Japan.
people.known_for_zh: 僧人，入唐师从玄奘学习，回国后传播法相宗。

people.name: En no Gyōja
people.known_for: Mountain ascetic regarded as the founder of Shugendō.
people.known_for_zh: 山林修行者，被尊为修验道的开山祖师。

Japan.name: Empress Genmei
Japan.note: Moved the capital to Heijō-kyō in 710.

Japan.name: Emperor Shōmu
Japan.note: Built Tōdai-ji and its Great Buddha.

Japan.name: Emperor Kanmu
Japan.note: Moved the capital to Nagaoka-kyō in 784 and Heian-kyō in 794.
Japan.note_zh: 784年迁都长冈京，794年迁都平安京。

people.name: Emperor Shōmu
people.known_for: Devout Buddhist emperor who founded provincial temples and built Tōdai-ji with its giant bronze Buddha.
people.known_for_zh: 笃信佛教的天皇，下令各国建国分寺，兴建东大寺并铸造大佛。

people.name: Empress Kōmyō
people.known_for: Consort of Shōmu, the first empress not of royal birth, who founded charity hospitals and gave the Shōsōin treasures.
people.known_for_zh: 圣武天皇的皇后，首位非皇族出身的皇后，设立施药院，捐献正仓院宝物。

people.name: Gyōki
people.known_for: Popular monk who built bridges and roads among the people and raised funds for the Great Buddha.
people.known_for_zh: 深受民众爱戴的僧人，带领百姓修桥筑路，并为东大寺大佛募集资金。

people.name: Rōben
people.known_for: Monk who became the first head of Tōdai-ji.
people.known_for_zh: 僧人，东大寺的首任别当（住持）。

people.name: Bodhisena
people.known_for: Indian monk who came to Japan via Tang China and performed the eye-opening ceremony of the Great Buddha in 752.
people.known_for_zh: 印度僧人，经唐朝来到日本，752年主持东大寺大佛开眼供养仪式。

people.name: Kibi no Makibi
people.known_for: Scholar who studied in Tang China for 17 years and brought back books on law, music and astronomy.
people.known_for_zh: 学者，在唐朝留学十七年，带回大量法律、音乐和天文书籍。

people.name: Abe no Nakamaro
people.known_for: Student who passed the Tang civil examination, served the Tang court for life and befriended Li Bai and Wang Wei.
people.known_for_zh: 遣唐留学生，考中唐朝科举，终身在唐为官，与李白、王维交好。

people.name: Prince Toneri
people.known_for: Prince who led the compilation of the Nihon Shoki, the first official history of Japan.
people.known_for_zh: 皇子，主持编纂日本第一部官修史书《日本书纪》。

people.name: Ō no Yasumaro
people.known_for: Court official who wrote down the Kojiki, Japan's oldest surviving book, from Hieda no Are's recitation.
people.known_for_zh: 朝廷官员，根据稗田阿礼的诵习撰录了日本现存最古老的书《古事记》。

people.name: Yamanoue no Okura
people.known_for: Man'yōshū poet who wrote with sympathy about poverty, children and the hardships of common people.
people.known_for_zh: 《万叶集》歌人，作品关注贫困、儿女和百姓疾苦。

people.name: Ōtomo no Tabito
people.known_for: Governor of Dazaifu and poet whose plum blossom party preface gave the name of the Reiwa era.
people.known_for_zh: 大宰帅、歌人，其梅花宴诗序成为“令和”年号的出处。

people.name: Ōtomo no Yakamochi
people.known_for: Poet believed to be the main compiler of the Man'yōshū, the oldest anthology of Japanese poetry.
people.known_for_zh: 歌人，被认为是日本最早的和歌总集《万叶集》的主要编纂者。

people.name: Tachibana no Moroe
people.known_for: Chief minister of Shōmu's court in the 740s.
people.known_for_zh: 740年代圣武天皇朝的首席大臣，主持朝政。

people.name: Fujiwara no Nakamaro
people.known_for: Powerful minister under Empress Kōken who renamed offices on the Tang model and died in a failed revolt.
people.known_for_zh: 孝谦天皇时期的权臣，仿唐朝改官名，后发动叛乱失败被杀。

people.name: Dōkyō
people.known_for: Monk favoured by Empress Shōtoku who almost became emperor before the court stopped him.
people.known_for_zh: 深得称德天皇宠信的僧人，一度几乎登上皇位，后被朝臣阻止。

Japan.name: Emperor Kanmu
Japan.note: Moved the capital to Heian-kyō in 794.

Japan.name: Emperor Seiwa
Japan.note: Fujiwara no Yoshifusa became regent in his reign.
Japan.note_zh: 在位期间藤原良房成为摄政。

Japan.name: Emperor Ichijō
Japan.note: Court of Murasaki Shikibu and Sei Shōnagon.
Japan.note_zh: 紫式部和清少纳言活跃于他的宫廷。

Japan.name: Emperor Shirakawa
Japan.note: Began rule by retired emperors (insei) after abdicating.

Japan.name: Emperor Antoku
Japan.note: Drowned at Dan-no-ura with the Taira.
Japan.note_zh: 随平氏在坛之浦投海而死。

people.name: Emperor Kanmu
people.known_for: Emperor who moved the capital to Heian-kyō (Kyoto) in 794 and sent armies against the Emishi of the north.
people.known_for_zh: 794年迁都平安京（京都），并派兵征讨东北的虾夷。

people.name: Sakanoue no Tamuramaro
people.known_for: General who subdued the Emishi of northern Honshu and became the model of the Seii Taishōgun.
people.known_for_zh: 武将，平定本州北部的虾夷，成为“征夷大将军”的典范。

people.name: Saichō
people.known_for: Monk who studied in Tang China and founded the Tendai school at Enryaku-ji on Mount Hiei.
people.known_for_zh: 僧人，入唐求法，回国后在比叡山延历寺创立天台宗。

people.name: Kūkai
people.known_for: Monk who brought esoteric Buddhism from Chang'an and founded the Shingon school on Mount Kōya; also a great calligrapher.
people.known_for_zh: 僧人，从长安带回密教，在高野山创立真言宗，也是著名书法家。

works.title: The Ten Stages of the Development of Mind

people.name: Ennin
people.known_for: Tendai monk whose diary of nine years in Tang China records the persecution of Buddhism in 845.
people.known_for_zh: 天台宗僧人，入唐九年，其日记记录了会昌灭佛等唐朝见闻。

works.title: Record of a Pilgrimage to China in Search of the Law

people.name: Fujiwara no Yoshifusa
people.known_for: First regent (sesshō) not of royal blood, who began the Fujiwara regency.
people.known_for_zh: 第一位非皇族出身的摄政，开创了藤原氏的摄关政治。

people.name: Ariwara no Narihira
people.known_for: Courtier poet and one of the Six Poetic Geniuses, traditionally the hero of The Tales of Ise.
people.known_for_zh: 贵族歌人，六歌仙之一，传统上被认为是《伊势物语》的主人公。

people.name: Ono no Komachi
people.known_for: Poet famed for her love poems and her beauty, the only woman among the Six Poetic Geniuses.
people.known_for_zh: 以恋歌和美貌闻名的女歌人，六歌仙中唯一的女性。

people.name: Sugawara no Michizane
people.known_for: Scholar-statesman who ended the missions to Tang, died in exile and is worshipped as Tenjin, god of learning.
people.known_for_zh: 学者兼政治家，建议停派遣唐使，后被贬死于太宰府，被奉为学问之神“天神”。

people.name: Ki no Tsurayuki
people.known_for: Poet who compiled the Kokinshū and wrote the Tosa Diary in kana.
people.known_for_zh: 歌人，主持编纂《古今和歌集》，用假名写作《土佐日记》。

people.name: Ono no Michikaze
people.known_for: Calligrapher who founded the native Japanese style of writing and is one of the Three Brush Traces.
people.known_for_zh: 书法家，开创了和样书法，为“三迹”之一。

people.name: Taira no Masakado
people.known_for: Warrior who seized the eastern provinces and proclaimed himself New Emperor before being killed in 940.
people.known_for_zh: 武士，占据关东诸国并自称“新皇”，940年兵败被杀。

people.name: Kūya
people.known_for: Wandering monk who spread the chanting of Amida's name among the common people of Kyoto.
people.known_for_zh: 游方僧人，在京都民间推广念佛，被称为“市圣”。

people.name: Abe no Seimei
people.known_for: Court diviner of yin-yang and astronomy, later a legendary figure in Japanese folklore.
people.known_for_zh: 朝廷的阴阳师，精通天文占卜，后来成为日本民间传说中的传奇人物。

people.name: Genshin
people.known_for: Tendai monk whose Essentials of Rebirth in the Pure Land shaped Japanese Pure Land belief.
people.known_for_zh: 天台宗僧人，所著《往生要集》深刻影响了日本的净土信仰。

people.name: Fujiwara no Michinaga
people.known_for: Regent at the height of Fujiwara power, father-in-law of three emperors.
people.known_for_zh: 藤原氏全盛时期的摄政，三位天皇的岳父。

people.name: Sei Shōnagon
people.known_for: Lady-in-waiting whose witty Pillow Book is a classic of Japanese prose.
people.known_for_zh: 宫廷女官，以机智的随笔《枕草子》成为日本散文经典作者。

people.name: Murasaki Shikibu
people.known_for: Lady-in-waiting who wrote The Tale of Genji, often called the world's first novel.
people.known_for_zh: 宫廷女官，著有《源氏物语》，常被称为世界上最早的长篇小说。

people.name: Fujiwara no Yorimichi
people.known_for: Regent for fifty years who built the Phoenix Hall of Byōdō-in at Uji.
people.known_for_zh: 担任摄政关白约五十年，在宇治兴建平等院凤凰堂。

people.name: Emperor Shirakawa
people.known_for: Emperor who after abdicating ruled as a cloistered emperor, starting the insei system.
people.known_for_zh: 退位后以上皇身份继续掌权，开创了院政。

people.name: Taira no Kiyomori
people.known_for: Warrior who became the first samurai to dominate the court, promoted trade with Song China and built Fukuhara.
people.known_for_zh: 第一个掌控朝廷的武士，推动日宋贸易，营建福原京。

people.name: Saigyō
people.known_for: Warrior turned monk whose poems of travel and nature are loved in Japan.
people.known_for_zh: 由武士出家的僧人歌人，其羁旅和自然之歌广受喜爱。

people.name: Hōnen
people.known_for: Monk who founded the Jōdo (Pure Land) school, teaching salvation by reciting Amida's name.
people.known_for_zh: 僧人，创立净土宗，主张专心念佛即可往生。

Imperial Japan (Fujiwara).name: Emperor Go-Toba
Imperial Japan (Fujiwara).note: Later led the failed Jōkyū War against the shogunate in 1221.
Imperial Japan (Fujiwara).note_zh: 后于1221年发动承久之乱讨伐幕府，失败。

Shogun Japan (Kamakura).name: Minamoto no Sanetomo
Shogun Japan (Kamakura).note: Assassinated; the Minamoto line ended with him.
Shogun Japan (Kamakura).note_zh: 遇刺身亡，源氏将军绝嗣。

Hōjō regents.name: Hōjō Tokimune
Hōjō regents.note: Led the defence against the Mongol invasions of 1274 and 1281.
Hōjō regents.note_zh: 领导抵御1274年和1281年的元军入侵。

Hōjō regents.name: Hōjō Takatoki
Hōjō regents.note: Remained the real head of the Hōjō until 1333.
Hōjō regents.note_zh: 此后至1333年仍是北条氏的实际首领。

people.name: Minamoto no Yoritomo
people.known_for: Founder of the Kamakura shogunate, Japan's first warrior government, after defeating the Taira.
people.known_for_zh: 击败平氏后建立镰仓幕府，开创了日本第一个武家政权。

people.name: Minamoto no Yoshitsune
people.known_for: Brilliant general who destroyed the Taira at Dan-no-ura in 1185, then was hunted down by his brother Yoritomo.
people.known_for_zh: 天才将领，1185年在坛之浦消灭平氏，后遭兄长源赖朝追杀。

people.name: Hōjō Masako
people.known_for: Widow of Yoritomo, the 'nun shogun' who held the shogunate together and rallied it in the Jōkyū War.
people.known_for_zh: 源赖朝的遗孀，被称为“尼将军”，维系幕府并在承久之乱中号召御家人。

people.name: Emperor Go-Toba
people.known_for: Retired emperor and poet who rose against the shogunate in 1221, lost and died in exile on the Oki Islands.
people.known_for_zh: 上皇兼歌人，1221年起兵讨伐幕府失败，被流放隐岐岛终老。

people.name: Hōjō Yasutoki
people.known_for: Regent who issued the Goseibai Shikimoku of 1232, the first law code of the warrior class.
people.known_for_zh: 执权，1232年制定《御成败式目》，这是第一部武家法典。

people.name: Hōjō Tokimune
people.known_for: Regent who rejected Kublai Khan's demands and led Japan through the Mongol invasions of 1274 and 1281.
people.known_for_zh: 执权，拒绝忽必烈的通好要求，领导日本抵御了1274年和1281年两次元军入侵。

people.name: Eisai
people.known_for: Monk who brought Rinzai Zen and the custom of drinking tea from Song China.
people.known_for_zh: 僧人，从宋朝传入临济宗和饮茶习俗。

people.name: Unkei
people.known_for: Sculptor of the Kei school whose lifelike guardian kings stand at the great gate of Tōdai-ji.
people.known_for_zh: 庆派佛像雕刻家，东大寺南大门的金刚力士像是其代表作。

people.name: Kamo no Chōmei
people.known_for: Recluse who wrote An Account of My Hut on the impermanence of all things.
people.known_for_zh: 隐士，所著《方丈记》抒写世事无常。

people.name: Jien
people.known_for: Tendai abbot and poet whose Gukanshō is the first Japanese work of historical interpretation.
people.known_for_zh: 天台座主兼歌人，所著《愚管抄》是日本第一部史论著作。

people.name: Fujiwara no Teika
people.known_for: Leading poet and critic who compiled the Shin Kokinshū and the Hyakunin Isshu.
people.known_for_zh: 著名歌人和歌论家，参与编纂《新古今和歌集》，选编《小仓百人一首》。

people.name: Shinran
people.known_for: Disciple of Hōnen who founded Jōdo Shinshū, the True Pure Land school.
people.known_for_zh: 法然的弟子，创立净土真宗。

people.name: Myōe
people.known_for: Kegon monk known for his strict practice and his record of dreams.
people.known_for_zh: 华严宗僧人，以严格修行和记录梦境的《梦记》闻名。

people.name: Dōgen
people.known_for: Monk who brought Sōtō Zen from Song China and founded Eihei-ji.
people.known_for_zh: 僧人，从宋朝传入曹洞宗，创建永平寺。

people.name: Lanxi Daolong
people.known_for: Chinese Chan monk who founded Kenchō-ji in Kamakura, the first pure Zen monastery in Japan.
people.known_for_zh: 南宋禅僧，东渡日本，在镰仓开创日本第一座纯粹禅寺建长寺。

people.name: Nichiren
people.known_for: Monk who taught faith in the Lotus Sutra alone and warned of foreign invasion.
people.known_for_zh: 僧人，主张专信《法华经》，并预言外敌入侵，创立日莲宗。

people.name: Mugaku Sogen
people.known_for: Chinese Chan monk invited by Hōjō Tokimune who founded Engaku-ji.
people.known_for_zh: 南宋禅僧，应北条时宗之邀东渡，开创圆觉寺。

people.name: Ippen
people.known_for: Wandering monk who spread dancing nenbutsu and founded the Ji school.
people.known_for_zh: 游行僧人，推广踊跃念佛，创立时宗。

people.name: Yoshida Kenkō
people.known_for: Monk and poet whose Essays in Idleness reflect on beauty and impermanence.
people.known_for_zh: 僧人兼歌人，所著随笔《徒然草》思考美与无常。

Japan.name: Emperor Go-Daigo
Japan.note: Led the Kenmu Restoration, then the Southern Court at Yoshino from 1336.
Japan.note_zh: 推行建武新政，1336年起在吉野建立南朝。

Japan.name: Emperor Go-Kameyama
Japan.note: Last Southern Court emperor; the courts were reunited in 1392.
Japan.note_zh: 南朝最后一位天皇，1392年南北朝合一。

Japan.name: Emperor Go-Komatsu
Japan.note: Reigned in the Northern Court from 1382; sole emperor from 1392.
Japan.note_zh: 1382年即位为北朝天皇，1392年起为唯一的天皇。

people.name: Emperor Go-Daigo
people.known_for: Emperor who overthrew the Kamakura shogunate, tried to restore imperial rule and then founded the Southern Court.
people.known_for_zh: 推翻镰仓幕府，推行建武新政，失败后在吉野建立南朝。

people.name: Musō Soseki
people.known_for: Rinzai Zen master and garden designer, adviser to Go-Daigo and the Ashikaga, creator of the Saihō-ji and Tenryū-ji gardens.
people.known_for_zh: 临济宗高僧和造园家，先后为后醍醐天皇和足利氏所尊崇，设计了西芳寺和天龙寺庭园。

people.name: Kusunoki Masashige
people.known_for: Loyal general of Go-Daigo who died at the Battle of Minatogawa, later a symbol of loyalty.
people.known_for_zh: 后醍醐天皇的忠臣名将，战死于凑川之战，后世被视为忠义的象征。

people.name: Kitabatake Chikafusa
people.known_for: Southern Court leader who wrote the Jinnō Shōtōki to argue the legitimacy of the Southern line.
people.known_for_zh: 南朝重臣，著《神皇正统记》论证南朝的正统性。

people.name: Sasaki Dōyo
people.known_for: Flamboyant warlord of the Ashikaga camp and patron of renga, tea and flower arranging.
people.known_for_zh: 足利阵营中作风豪奢的武将，赞助连歌、茶道和花道。

people.name: Nitta Yoshisada
people.known_for: General who captured Kamakura in 1333, ending the Hōjō, and fought for the Southern Court.
people.known_for_zh: 1333年攻陷镰仓、消灭北条氏的武将，后为南朝作战。

people.name: Ashikaga Takauji
people.known_for: Warrior who turned against Go-Daigo, set up the Northern Court and founded the Ashikaga shogunate.
people.known_for_zh: 背叛后醍醐天皇，拥立北朝，建立室町幕府。

people.name: Ashikaga Tadayoshi
people.known_for: Brother of Takauji who ran the early shogunate's government until their quarrel in the Kannō Disturbance.
people.known_for_zh: 足利尊氏之弟，主持幕府初期政务，后与兄长在观应之乱中反目。

people.name: Imagawa Sadayo
people.known_for: Shogunal deputy who won Kyushu back from the Southern Court and wrote poetry and history.
people.known_for_zh: 幕府九州探题，为北朝收复九州，也是歌人和史家。

people.name: Hosokawa Yoriyuki
people.known_for: Deputy shogun (kanrei) who guided the young Yoshimitsu.
people.known_for_zh: 管领，辅佐年幼的足利义满。

people.name: Kan'ami
people.known_for: Actor and playwright who created Noh theatre and won the patronage of Yoshimitsu.
people.known_for_zh: 演员和剧作家，创立能乐，得到足利义满的赞助。

people.name: Zekkai Chūshin
people.known_for: Zen monk who studied in Ming China and was a master of Chinese poetry of the Five Mountains.
people.known_for_zh: 禅僧，曾入明求法，是五山文学中汉诗的代表人物。

people.name: Ashikaga Yoshimitsu
people.known_for: Shogun who reunited the courts in 1392, opened tally trade with Ming China and built the Golden Pavilion.
people.known_for_zh: 将军，1392年实现南北朝合一，开展与明朝的勘合贸易，兴建金阁寺。

people.name: Zeami
people.known_for: Son of Kan'ami who perfected Noh and wrote its classic plays and treatises.
people.known_for_zh: 观阿弥之子，使能乐臻于完善，写下许多经典剧目和艺术论著。

people.name: Ikkyū
people.known_for: Eccentric Zen monk and poet who mocked the formalism of the Zen establishment.
people.known_for_zh: 特立独行的禅僧和诗人，讥讽禅林的形式主义，后世成为“一休”故事的原型。

Japan (Warring States).name: Ashikaga Yoshiaki
Japan (Warring States).note: Installed by Oda Nobunaga, who drove him from Kyoto in 1573.
Japan (Warring States).note_zh: 由织田信长拥立，1573年被信长逐出京都。

people.name: Ashikaga Yoshimasa
people.known_for: Shogun whose succession quarrel set off the Ōnin War; he built the Silver Pavilion and fostered Higashiyama culture.
people.known_for_zh: 将军，继承人之争引发应仁之乱，兴建银阁寺，倡导东山文化。

people.name: Hosokawa Katsumoto
people.known_for: Kanrei who led the Eastern Army in the Ōnin War.
people.known_for_zh: 管领，应仁之乱中东军的统帅。

people.name: Yamana Sōzen
people.known_for: Warlord who led the Western Army in the Ōnin War.
people.known_for_zh: 大名，应仁之乱中西军的统帅。

people.name: Sesshū
people.known_for: Zen monk-painter who studied in Ming China and became the greatest master of Japanese ink painting.
people.known_for_zh: 禅僧画家，曾入明学画，成为日本水墨画的最高大师。

people.name: Sōgi
people.known_for: Master of linked verse (renga) who travelled widely through the warring provinces.
people.known_for_zh: 连歌大师，在战乱中游历各地。

people.name: Murata Jukō
people.known_for: Founder of the wabi style of tea ceremony.
people.known_for_zh: 茶人，被视为侘茶的开创者。

people.name: Rennyo
people.known_for: Head of Hongan-ji who turned Jōdo Shinshū into a mass movement whose followers formed the Ikkō leagues.
people.known_for_zh: 本愿寺法主，使净土真宗成为大众教团，信徒结成一向一揆。

people.name: Hōjō Sōun
people.known_for: Warrior of modest rank who seized Izu and Sagami, often called the first Sengoku daimyō.
people.known_for_zh: 出身不高的武士，夺取伊豆和相模，常被称为第一个战国大名。

people.name: Kanō Motonobu
people.known_for: Painter who built the Kanō school into the leading workshop of Japanese painting.
people.known_for_zh: 画家，使狩野派成为日本画坛最重要的流派。

people.name: Takeno Jōō
people.known_for: Merchant tea master of Sakai who developed wabi tea and taught Sen no Rikyū.
people.known_for_zh: 堺的商人茶人，发展了侘茶，是千利休的老师。

people.name: Mōri Motonari
people.known_for: Warlord who rose from a small lord to master of the Chūgoku region, famed for the lesson of the three arrows.
people.known_for_zh: 由小领主崛起为中国地方霸主的大名，以“三矢之训”闻名。

people.name: Saitō Dōsan
people.known_for: Oil merchant's son who seized Mino province, the classic example of the low overthrowing the high.
people.known_for_zh: 夺取美浓国的大名，是“下克上”的典型人物。

people.name: Ōuchi Yoshitaka
people.known_for: Lord of Yamaguchi who ran the Ming trade and received Francis Xavier.
people.known_for_zh: 山口的大名，经营对明贸易，接待过沙勿略。

people.name: Imagawa Yoshimoto
people.known_for: Powerful daimyō of Suruga killed by Oda Nobunaga's surprise attack at Okehazama.
people.known_for_zh: 骏河的强大大名，在桶狭间之战中被织田信长奇袭身亡。

people.name: Miyoshi Nagayoshi
people.known_for: Warlord who controlled Kyoto and the shogunate in the 1550s.
people.known_for_zh: 大名，1550年代控制京都和幕府。

people.name: Takeda Shingen
people.known_for: Daimyō of Kai famed for his cavalry and his battles with Uesugi Kenshin at Kawanakajima.
people.known_for_zh: 甲斐国大名，以骑兵著称，与上杉谦信在川中岛多次交战。

people.name: Uesugi Kenshin
people.known_for: Daimyō of Echigo, devout Buddhist and rival of Takeda Shingen.
people.known_for_zh: 越后国大名，笃信佛教，武田信玄的宿敌。

Oda and Toyotomi regimes.name: Oda Nobunaga
Oda and Toyotomi regimes.note: Entered Kyoto in 1568 and deposed the last shogun in 1573; killed at Honnō-ji.
Oda and Toyotomi regimes.note_zh: 1568年进入京都，1573年废黜末代将军，死于本能寺之变。

Oda and Toyotomi regimes.name: Toyotomi Hideyoshi
Oda and Toyotomi regimes.note: Kampaku from 1585; completed the unification in 1590.

Oda and Toyotomi regimes.name: Toyotomi Hideyori
Oda and Toyotomi regimes.note: Under a council of five regents led by Tokugawa Ieyasu; lost real power after Sekigahara.
Oda and Toyotomi regimes.note_zh: 由德川家康等五大老辅政，关原之战后失去实权。

people.name: Oda Nobunaga
people.known_for: Warlord who began the unification of Japan, used massed muskets and built Azuchi Castle before dying at Honnō-ji.
people.known_for_zh: 开启日本统一进程的大名，大量使用火枪，兴建安土城，后死于本能寺之变。

people.name: Toyotomi Hideyoshi
people.known_for: Peasant-born general who completed the unification of Japan, surveyed the land, disarmed peasants and invaded Korea.
people.known_for_zh: 出身农民的武将，完成日本统一，推行太阁检地和刀狩令，并出兵侵略朝鲜。

people.name: Akechi Mitsuhide
people.known_for: Nobunaga's general who turned on him at Honnō-ji and was defeated by Hideyoshi days later.
people.known_for_zh: 织田信长的部将，发动本能寺之变，数日后被丰臣秀吉击败。

people.name: Shibata Katsuie
people.known_for: Nobunaga's senior general, defeated by Hideyoshi at Shizugatake.
people.known_for_zh: 织田信长的首席家臣，在贱岳之战中败于丰臣秀吉。

people.name: Takeda Katsuyori
people.known_for: Son of Shingen whose cavalry was crushed by Oda musketeers at Nagashino in 1575.
people.known_for_zh: 武田信玄之子，1575年在长篠之战中被织田军的火枪队击溃。

people.name: Sen no Rikyū
people.known_for: Tea master to Nobunaga and Hideyoshi who perfected the wabi tea ceremony; ordered by Hideyoshi to kill himself.
people.known_for_zh: 织田信长和丰臣秀吉的茶头，集侘茶之大成，后被秀吉命令切腹。

people.name: Kanō Eitoku
people.known_for: Painter of bold gold-leaf screens and walls for the castles of Nobunaga and Hideyoshi.
people.known_for_zh: 画家，为信长和秀吉的城郭绘制气势恢宏的金碧障壁画。

people.name: Hasegawa Tōhaku
people.known_for: Painter famous for the misty Pine Trees screens, a masterpiece of ink painting.
people.known_for_zh: 画家，以水墨画杰作《松林图屏风》闻名。

people.name: Luís Fróis
people.known_for: Jesuit missionary who knew Nobunaga and wrote a detailed History of Japan.
people.known_for_zh: 耶稣会传教士，结识织田信长，撰写了详尽的《日本史》。

people.name: Alessandro Valignano
people.known_for: Jesuit visitor who organised the mission in Japan and sent the Tenshō embassy to Europe.
people.known_for_zh: 耶稣会远东视察员，整顿日本传教事业，派遣天正遣欧使节。

people.name: Itō Mancio
people.known_for: Leader of the Tenshō embassy of four Japanese boys who met the Pope in Rome in 1585.
people.known_for_zh: 天正遣欧使节团的正使，1585年在罗马觐见教皇。

people.name: Ishida Mitsunari
people.known_for: Hideyoshi's administrator who led the Western Army and lost at Sekigahara in 1600.
people.known_for_zh: 丰臣秀吉的重臣，率西军在1600年的关原之战中战败。

people.name: Katō Kiyomasa
people.known_for: Hideyoshi's general in the invasion of Korea and builder of Kumamoto Castle.
people.known_for_zh: 丰臣秀吉的武将，参与侵朝战争，修筑熊本城。

people.name: Konishi Yukinaga
people.known_for: Christian general who led the vanguard of the invasion of Korea in 1592.
people.known_for_zh: 信奉天主教的武将，1592年率先锋入侵朝鲜。

people.name: Date Masamune
people.known_for: One-eyed daimyō of Tōhoku who founded Sendai and sent an embassy to Spain and Rome.
people.known_for_zh: 东北地区的独眼大名，建立仙台城下町，派遣使节前往西班牙和罗马。

Tokugawa shogunate.name: Tokugawa Yoshinobu
Tokugawa shogunate.note: Returned power to the emperor in 1867.

people.name: Tokugawa Ieyasu
people.known_for: Won the Battle of Sekigahara in 1600 and founded the Tokugawa shogunate, which ruled Japan for over 260 years.
people.known_for_zh: 1600年赢得关原之战，建立统治日本二百六十余年的江户幕府。

people.name: Tokugawa Iemitsu
people.known_for: Third shogun who required daimyō to live in Edo in alternate years and closed Japan to most foreigners.
people.known_for_zh: 第三代将军，确立参勤交代制度，推行锁国政策。

people.name: Miyamoto Musashi
people.known_for: Undefeated swordsman and ink painter who wrote The Book of Five Rings.
people.known_for_zh: 未尝一败的剑客，也是水墨画家，著有《五轮书》。

people.name: Hayashi Razan
people.known_for: Neo-Confucian scholar who served the first four shoguns and made Zhu Xi's teaching the official doctrine.
people.known_for_zh: 朱子学者，先后侍奉四代将军，使朱子学成为幕府的官方学问。

people.name: Amakusa Shirō
people.known_for: Young Christian leader of the Shimabara Rebellion, after which the shogunate sealed the country.
people.known_for_zh: 岛原之乱中天主教起义军的少年领袖，此后幕府彻底实行锁国。

people.name: Tawaraya Sōtatsu
people.known_for: Painter who founded the decorative Rinpa style; famous for the Wind God and Thunder God screens.
people.known_for_zh: 画家，开创琳派装饰画风，以《风神雷神图》闻名。

people.name: Ihara Saikaku
people.known_for: Osaka writer of lively stories of townsmen's love and money.
people.known_for_zh: 大阪作家，生动描写町人的情爱与金钱。

works.title: The Life of an Amorous Man

people.name: Seki Takakazu
people.known_for: Mathematician who founded traditional Japanese mathematics (wasan) and discovered determinants.
people.known_for_zh: 数学家，和算的奠基人，独立发现了行列式。

people.name: Matsuo Bashō
people.known_for: Greatest master of haiku, whose travel journals include The Narrow Road to the Deep North.
people.known_for_zh: 最伟大的俳句大师，代表作有游记《奥之细道》。

works.title: The Narrow Road to the Deep North

people.name: Chikamatsu Monzaemon
people.known_for: Playwright for puppet theatre and kabuki, called the Shakespeare of Japan.
people.known_for_zh: 人形净琉璃和歌舞伎剧作家，被称为“日本的莎士比亚”。

people.name: Arai Hakuseki
people.known_for: Confucian adviser to the shoguns who reformed the currency and wrote on the West.
people.known_for_zh: 辅佐将军的儒学者，整顿货币，著有介绍西方的著作。

people.name: Ogata Kōrin
people.known_for: Rinpa painter of the Irises screens and Red and White Plum Blossoms.
people.known_for_zh: 琳派画家，代表作有《燕子花图》和《红白梅图》。

people.name: Ogyū Sorai
people.known_for: Confucian thinker who called for a return to the ancient classics and practical statecraft.
people.known_for_zh: 儒学家，主张回归古代经典，重视经世致用。

people.name: Tokugawa Yoshimune
people.known_for: Eighth shogun whose Kyōhō Reforms restored finances and who allowed Western books to be imported.
people.known_for_zh: 第八代将军，推行享保改革整顿财政，放宽西方书籍的进口。

people.name: Yosa Buson
people.known_for: Haiku poet and painter, one of the three great masters of haiku.
people.known_for_zh: 俳人兼画家，与芭蕉、一茶并称俳句三大家。

people.name: Tanuma Okitsugu
people.known_for: Senior councillor who promoted commerce and merchant guilds, later blamed for corruption.
people.known_for_zh: 老中，大力发展商业和株仲间，后被指责贿赂成风。

people.name: Hiraga Gennai
people.known_for: Inventive Dutch-studies scholar who built an electrostatic generator and wrote popular fiction.
people.known_for_zh: 兰学家和发明家，制作了摩擦起电器，也写通俗小说。

people.name: Motoori Norinaga
people.known_for: Leading scholar of National Learning who spent 35 years on a commentary on the Kojiki.
people.known_for_zh: 国学集大成者，用三十五年写成《古事记传》。

people.name: Sugita Genpaku
people.known_for: Physician who translated a Dutch anatomy book, launching Western medicine in Japan.
people.known_for_zh: 医生，翻译荷兰解剖学著作，开启了西洋医学在日本的传播。

people.name: Inō Tadataka
people.known_for: Surveyor who walked the coasts of Japan for 17 years to make the first accurate map of the country.
people.known_for_zh: 测量家，花十七年徒步测量日本沿海，绘制出第一幅精确的日本全图。

people.name: Kitagawa Utamaro
people.known_for: Ukiyo-e master of portraits of beautiful women.
people.known_for_zh: 浮世绘大师，以美人画闻名。

people.name: Matsudaira Sadanobu
people.known_for: Chief councillor who led the austere Kansei Reforms.
people.known_for_zh: 老中首座，推行厉行节俭的宽政改革。

people.name: Katsushika Hokusai
people.known_for: Ukiyo-e artist whose Great Wave off Kanagawa is one of the most famous images in the world.
people.known_for_zh: 浮世绘画家，其《神奈川冲浪里》是世界上最著名的图画之一。

people.name: Kobayashi Issa
people.known_for: Haiku poet known for tender poems about small creatures and his own hardships.
people.known_for_zh: 俳人，以描写小动物和自身困苦的温情俳句闻名。

people.name: Ōshio Heihachirō
people.known_for: Former Osaka official and Wang Yangming scholar who led a revolt for famine victims in 1837.
people.known_for_zh: 大阪前町奉行所与力、阳明学者，1837年为救济饥民起兵。

people.name: Utagawa Hiroshige
people.known_for: Ukiyo-e landscape artist known for The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō.
people.known_for_zh: 浮世绘风景画家，以《东海道五十三次》闻名。

works.title: The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō
One Hundred Famous Views of Edo

people.name: Ii Naosuke
people.known_for: Great Elder who signed the treaties with the West without imperial consent and was assassinated in 1860.
people.known_for_zh: 大老，未经天皇批准与西方签订条约，1860年在樱田门外遇刺。

people.name: Yoshida Shōin
people.known_for: Teacher whose small school in Hagi trained many leaders of the Meiji Restoration; executed in 1859.
people.known_for_zh: 教育家，在萩开办松下村塾，培养了许多明治维新领导人，1859年被处死。

people.name: Sakamoto Ryōma
people.known_for: Tosa samurai who brokered the Satsuma-Chōshū alliance and planned the return of power to the emperor; assassinated.
people.known_for_zh: 土佐藩士，促成萨长同盟，策划大政奉还，后遇刺身亡。

people.name: Emperor Meiji
people.known_for: Emperor in whose name Japan abolished the shogunate and became a modern industrial power.
people.known_for_zh: 以其名义推翻幕府、使日本成为近代工业强国的天皇。

people.name: Iwakura Tomomi
people.known_for: Court noble who helped plan the Restoration and led the Iwakura Mission to America and Europe.
people.known_for_zh: 公卿，参与策划明治维新，率岩仓使节团出访欧美。

people.name: Saigō Takamori
people.known_for: Satsuma leader of the Restoration who later led the Satsuma Rebellion and died at Shiroyama.
people.known_for_zh: 萨摩藩出身的维新元勋，后发动西南战争，战死于城山。

people.name: Ōkubo Toshimichi
people.known_for: Restoration leader who abolished the domains and drove industrial growth; assassinated in 1878.
people.known_for_zh: 维新三杰之一，推行废藩置县和殖产兴业，1878年遇刺。

people.name: Kido Takayoshi
people.known_for: Chōshū leader of the Restoration who drafted the Charter Oath.
people.known_for_zh: 长州藩出身的维新三杰之一，参与起草《五条御誓文》。

people.name: Katsu Kaishū
people.known_for: Naval officer of the shogunate who negotiated the peaceful surrender of Edo in 1868.
people.known_for_zh: 幕府海军将领，1868年谈判实现江户无血开城。

people.name: Fukuzawa Yukichi
people.known_for: Educator who founded Keio University and spread Western ideas of liberty and learning.
people.known_for_zh: 启蒙思想家和教育家，创办庆应义塾，传播西方自由和学问思想。

works.title: An Outline of a Theory of Civilization

people.name: Itagaki Taisuke
people.known_for: Leader of the Freedom and People's Rights Movement and founder of Japan's first political party.
people.known_for_zh: 自由民权运动领袖，创立日本第一个政党自由党。

people.name: Ōkuma Shigenobu
people.known_for: Twice prime minister and founder of Waseda University.
people.known_for_zh: 两度出任首相，创办早稻田大学。

people.name: Yamagata Aritomo
people.known_for: Founder of the modern Japanese army and conscription, twice prime minister.
people.known_for_zh: 日本近代陆军和征兵制的创建者，两度出任首相。

people.name: Shibusawa Eiichi
people.known_for: Businessman who founded hundreds of companies and Japan's first modern bank.
people.known_for_zh: 实业家，创办数百家企业和日本第一家近代银行。

people.name: Itō Hirobumi
people.known_for: First prime minister who drafted the Meiji Constitution; Resident-General of Korea, killed by An Jung-geun.
people.known_for_zh: 首任内阁总理大臣，主持制定明治宪法，后任韩国统监，被安重根刺杀。

people.name: Mutsu Munemitsu
people.known_for: Foreign minister who ended extraterritoriality and negotiated the Treaty of Shimonoseki.
people.known_for_zh: 外务大臣，废除治外法权，主持签订《马关条约》。

people.name: Tōgō Heihachirō
people.known_for: Admiral who destroyed the Russian fleet at the Battle of Tsushima in 1905.
people.known_for_zh: 海军将领，1905年在对马海战中歼灭俄国舰队。

people.name: Nogi Maresuke
people.known_for: General who took Port Arthur in the Russo-Japanese War and killed himself on Emperor Meiji's death.
people.known_for_zh: 陆军将领，日俄战争中攻陷旅顺，明治天皇去世时殉死。

people.name: Kitasato Shibasaburō
people.known_for: Bacteriologist who developed serum therapy for tetanus and found the plague bacillus.
people.known_for_zh: 细菌学家，开创破伤风血清疗法，发现鼠疫杆菌。

people.name: Takamine Jōkichi
people.known_for: Chemist who first isolated adrenaline.
people.known_for_zh: 化学家，首次分离出肾上腺素。

people.name: Mori Ōgai
people.known_for: Army doctor and novelist, a founder of modern Japanese literature.
people.known_for_zh: 陆军军医兼小说家，日本近代文学的奠基人之一。

people.name: Nitobe Inazō
people.known_for: Educator who wrote Bushido: The Soul of Japan and later served the League of Nations.
people.known_for_zh: 教育家，著有《武士道》，后任国际联盟副秘书长。

people.name: Okakura Kakuzō
people.known_for: Art scholar who defended traditional Asian art and wrote The Book of Tea.
people.known_for_zh: 美术学者，致力于保护东方传统美术，著有《茶之书》。

people.name: Tsuda Umeko
people.known_for: Pioneer of women's education who studied in America as a child and founded Tsuda College.
people.known_for_zh: 女子教育先驱，幼年留学美国，创办津田塾大学。

people.name: Natsume Sōseki
people.known_for: Novelist regarded as the greatest writer of modern Japan.
people.known_for_zh: 小说家，被视为日本近代最伟大的作家。

people.name: Masaoka Shiki
people.known_for: Poet who renewed haiku and tanka for the modern age.
people.known_for_zh: 诗人，革新了俳句和短歌。

people.name: Kōtoku Shūsui
people.known_for: Socialist and anarchist executed after the High Treason Incident.
people.known_for_zh: 社会主义和无政府主义者，在大逆事件后被处死。

people.name: Higuchi Ichiyō
people.known_for: Woman writer of short stories about the poor quarters of Tokyo.
people.known_for_zh: 女作家，以描写东京下层社会的短篇小说闻名。

people.name: Yosano Akiko
people.known_for: Poet whose passionate tanka collection Tangled Hair shocked and thrilled readers; also opposed the Russo-Japanese War.
people.known_for_zh: 诗人，其热情奔放的短歌集《乱发》轰动文坛，曾写诗反对日俄战争。

people.name: Ishikawa Takuboku
people.known_for: Tanka poet of everyday life and poverty who died young.
people.known_for_zh: 短歌诗人，书写日常生活与贫困，英年早逝。

Empire of Japan.name: Yoshihito
Empire of Japan.note: Crown Prince Hirohito acted as regent from 1921.

people.name: Hara Takashi
people.known_for: First commoner prime minister, who formed the first true party cabinet in 1918; assassinated.
people.known_for_zh: 第一位平民出身的首相，1918年组建第一个真正的政党内阁，后遇刺。

people.name: Katō Takaaki
people.known_for: Foreign minister behind the Twenty-One Demands on China, later prime minister who passed universal male suffrage.
people.known_for_zh: 外务大臣时向中国提出“二十一条”，任首相时通过男子普选法。

people.name: Yokoyama Taikan
people.known_for: Leading painter of modern Nihonga.
people.known_for_zh: 近代日本画的代表画家。

people.name: Kitarō Nishida
people.known_for: Philosopher who founded the Kyoto School, blending Zen and Western philosophy.
people.known_for_zh: 哲学家，京都学派创始人，融合禅与西方哲学。

people.name: Kōtarō Honda
people.known_for: Metallurgist who invented KS steel, a powerful magnet steel.
people.known_for_zh: 冶金学家，发明了强磁性的KS钢。

people.name: Umetaro Suzuki
people.known_for: Agricultural chemist who extracted the first vitamin, from rice bran.
people.known_for_zh: 农业化学家，从米糠中提取出最早的维生素。

people.name: Kunio Yanagita
people.known_for: Founder of Japanese folklore studies.
people.known_for_zh: 日本民俗学的创始人。

people.name: Hideyo Noguchi
people.known_for: Bacteriologist who identified the syphilis organism in the brain; died of yellow fever in Africa.
people.known_for_zh: 细菌学家，在病人脑中发现梅毒螺旋体，后在非洲研究黄热病时染病去世。

people.name: Sakuzō Yoshino
people.known_for: Political scientist whose call for government for the people inspired Taishō Democracy.
people.known_for_zh: 政治学家，提出“民本主义”，是大正民主运动的理论旗手。

people.name: Naoya Shiga
people.known_for: Novelist of the Shirakaba group, called the god of the novel.
people.known_for_zh: 白桦派小说家，被誉为“小说之神”。

people.name: Ōsugi Sakae
people.known_for: Anarchist murdered by military police after the Great Kantō Earthquake.
people.known_for_zh: 无政府主义者，关东大地震后被宪兵杀害。

people.name: Hiratsuka Raichō
people.known_for: Feminist who founded the women's magazine Seitō with the words 'In the beginning, woman was the sun'.
people.known_for_zh: 女权运动家，创办女性杂志《青鞜》，写下“元始，女性是太阳”。

people.name: Ryūnosuke Akutagawa
people.known_for: Master of the short story whose name is given to Japan's top literary prize.
people.known_for_zh: 短篇小说大师，日本最重要的文学奖芥川奖以他命名。

people.name: Kenji Miyazawa
people.known_for: Poet and children's writer from rural Iwate.
people.known_for_zh: 来自岩手乡村的诗人和童话作家。

Empire of Japan.name: Hirohito
Empire of Japan.note: Under the 1947 constitution he became the symbol of the state.
Empire of Japan.note_zh: 1947年新宪法施行后成为国家象征。

people.name: Emperor Shōwa
people.known_for: Emperor through Japan's wars of aggression and defeat in 1945, who then became a constitutional symbol.
people.known_for_zh: 在位期间经历了日本的侵略战争和1945年战败，战后成为宪法规定的国家象征。

people.name: Hideki Tojo
people.known_for: General and wartime prime minister who ordered the attack on Pearl Harbor; executed as a war criminal.
people.known_for_zh: 陆军将领，战时首相，下令偷袭珍珠港，战后作为甲级战犯被处死。

people.name: Isoroku Yamamoto
people.known_for: Admiral who planned the attack on Pearl Harbor.
people.known_for_zh: 海军将领，策划了偷袭珍珠港。

people.name: Kanji Ishiwara
people.known_for: Army officer who plotted the Mukden Incident of 1931 and the seizure of Manchuria.
people.known_for_zh: 陆军军官，策划了1931年九一八事变和侵占中国东北。

people.name: Fumimaro Konoe
people.known_for: Prime minister when Japan launched full-scale war on China in 1937.
people.known_for_zh: 1937年日本全面侵华时的首相。

people.name: Shigeru Yoshida
people.known_for: Post-war prime minister who signed the San Francisco Peace Treaty and set Japan's course of economic growth.
people.known_for_zh: 战后首相，签订《旧金山和约》，确定了日本以经济发展为重心的路线。

people.name: Nobusuke Kishi
people.known_for: Prime minister who revised the US-Japan Security Treaty in 1960 amid mass protests.
people.known_for_zh: 首相，1960年在大规模抗议中修订《日美安保条约》。

people.name: Hayato Ikeda
people.known_for: Prime minister of the Income Doubling Plan and the 1964 Tokyo Olympics.
people.known_for_zh: 首相，推出“国民收入倍增计划”，主持1964年东京奥运会。

people.name: Eisaku Satō
people.known_for: Prime minister who secured the return of Okinawa and received the Nobel Peace Prize.
people.known_for_zh: 首相，实现冲绳回归，获诺贝尔和平奖。

people.name: Kakuei Tanaka
people.known_for: Prime minister who normalised relations with the People's Republic of China in 1972.
people.known_for_zh: 首相，1972年实现中日邦交正常化。

people.name: Yasuhiro Nakasone
people.known_for: Prime minister of the 1980s who privatised the national railways.
people.known_for_zh: 1980年代的首相，推行国铁民营化。

people.name: Hideki Yukawa
people.known_for: Physicist who predicted the meson and became Japan's first Nobel laureate in 1949.
people.known_for_zh: 物理学家，预言了介子的存在，1949年成为日本第一位诺贝尔奖得主。

people.name: Sin-Itiro Tomonaga
people.known_for: Physicist who shared the 1965 Nobel Prize for quantum electrodynamics.
people.known_for_zh: 物理学家，因量子电动力学研究获1965年诺贝尔物理学奖。

people.name: Jun'ichirō Tanizaki
people.known_for: Novelist of beauty and desire whose essay In Praise of Shadows is a classic of Japanese aesthetics.
people.known_for_zh: 唯美派小说家，随笔《阴翳礼赞》是日本美学的经典。

people.name: Yasunari Kawabata
people.known_for: Novelist who in 1968 became the first Japanese winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature.
people.known_for_zh: 小说家，1968年成为第一位获诺贝尔文学奖的日本人。

people.name: Osamu Dazai
people.known_for: Novelist of despair and self-mockery.
people.known_for_zh: 以绝望和自嘲为基调的小说家。

people.name: Yukio Mishima
people.known_for: Novelist who killed himself after a failed call for a military coup.
people.known_for_zh: 小说家，号召自卫队政变失败后切腹自杀。

works.title: The Temple of the Golden Pavilion

people.name: Kenzaburō Ōe
people.known_for: Novelist of post-war Japan and the atomic bomb, Nobel laureate in 1994.
people.known_for_zh: 书写战后日本和原子弹问题的小说家，1994年获诺贝尔文学奖。

people.name: Yasujirō Ozu
people.known_for: Film director of quiet family dramas.
people.known_for_zh: 电影导演，以平静细腻的家庭剧闻名。

people.name: Akira Kurosawa
people.known_for: Film director whose samurai epics influenced cinema worldwide.
people.known_for_zh: 电影导演，其武士史诗影响了世界电影。

people.name: Kenzō Tange
people.known_for: Architect of the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park and the Yoyogi stadium.
people.known_for_zh: 建筑师，设计了广岛和平纪念公园和代代木体育馆。

people.name: Osamu Tezuka
people.known_for: The 'god of manga' who created Astro Boy and shaped modern manga and anime.
people.known_for_zh: 被誉为“漫画之神”，创作了《铁臂阿童木》，奠定了现代漫画和动画的基础。

people.name: Hibari Misora
people.known_for: Singer and actress, the queen of post-war Japanese popular song.
people.known_for_zh: 歌手和演员，战后日本流行歌坛的女王。

people.name: Kōnosuke Matsushita
people.known_for: Founder of Panasonic, admired in Japan as the god of management.
people.known_for_zh: 松下电器创始人，被誉为“经营之神”。

people.name: Soichiro Honda
people.known_for: Engineer who founded Honda.
people.known_for_zh: 工程师，本田公司的创始人。

people.name: Akio Morita
people.known_for: Co-founder of Sony who brought Japanese electronics to the world.
people.known_for_zh: 索尼联合创始人，将日本电子产品推向世界。

Japan.name: Akihito
Japan.note: Abdicated in 2019, the first abdication in two centuries.
Japan.note_zh: 2019年退位，为二百年来首次天皇生前退位。

people.name: Tomiichi Murayama
people.known_for: Socialist prime minister whose 1995 statement apologised for Japan's colonial rule and aggression.
people.known_for_zh: 社会党出身的首相，1995年发表谈话，就日本的殖民统治和侵略表示道歉。

people.name: Junichiro Koizumi
people.known_for: Prime minister who privatised Japan Post.
people.known_for_zh: 首相，推行邮政民营化改革。

people.name: Shinzo Abe
people.known_for: Longest-serving prime minister, known for 'Abenomics'; assassinated in 2022.
people.known_for_zh: 任期最长的日本首相，推行“安倍经济学”，2022年遇刺身亡。

people.name: Sadako Ogata
people.known_for: UN High Commissioner for Refugees in the 1990s.
people.known_for_zh: 1990年代担任联合国难民事务高级专员。

people.name: Masatoshi Koshiba
people.known_for: Physicist who detected neutrinos from a supernova; Nobel Prize 2002.
people.known_for_zh: 物理学家，探测到超新星中微子，获2002年诺贝尔物理学奖。

people.name: Isamu Akasaki
people.known_for: Engineer who helped invent the blue LED; Nobel Prize 2014.
people.known_for_zh: 工程师，参与发明蓝色发光二极管，获2014年诺贝尔物理学奖。

people.name: Shinya Yamanaka
people.known_for: Biologist who created induced pluripotent stem cells; Nobel Prize 2012.
people.known_for_zh: 生物学家，培育出诱导多能干细胞，获2012年诺贝尔生理学或医学奖。

people.name: Hayao Miyazaki
people.known_for: Animator and co-founder of Studio Ghibli.
people.known_for_zh: 动画导演，吉卜力工作室联合创始人。

people.name: Haruki Murakami
people.known_for: Novelist read around the world.
people.known_for_zh: 作品在世界各地广受欢迎的小说家。

people.name: Tadao Ando
people.known_for: Self-taught architect of concrete and light; Pritzker Prize 1995.
people.known_for_zh: 自学成才的建筑师，以清水混凝土和光影著称，获1995年普利兹克奖。

people.name: Akira Toriyama
people.known_for: Manga artist who created Dragon Ball.
people.known_for_zh: 漫画家，创作了《龙珠》。

people.name: Ryuichi Sakamoto
people.known_for: Composer and musician who won an Oscar for The Last Emperor.
people.known_for_zh: 作曲家和音乐人，凭《末代皇帝》获奥斯卡最佳原创配乐奖。

people.name: Seiji Ozawa
people.known_for: Conductor of the Boston Symphony Orchestra for 29 years.
people.known_for_zh: 指挥家，执掌波士顿交响乐团二十九年。

people.name: Ichiro Suzuki
people.known_for: Baseball player with record hits in Japan and the US Major Leagues.
people.known_for_zh: 棒球运动员，在日本和美国职业棒球大联盟创造了安打纪录。

people.name: Yoshihide Suga
people.known_for: Prime minister in 2020 and 2021 who held the delayed Tokyo Olympics.
people.known_for_zh: 2020年至2021年任首相，举办了延期的东京奥运会。

people.name: Fumio Kishida
people.known_for: Prime minister from 2021 to 2024 who raised defence spending.
people.known_for_zh: 2021年至2024年任首相，大幅增加防卫开支。

people.name: Shigeru Ishiba
people.known_for: Prime minister from 2024 to 2025.
people.known_for_zh: 2024年至2025年任日本首相。

people.name: Sanae Takaichi
people.known_for: First woman prime minister of Japan, from 2025.
people.known_for_zh: 2025年起任首相，是日本第一位女首相。

people.name: Shohei Ohtani
people.known_for: Baseball player who excels as both pitcher and hitter in the US Major Leagues.
people.known_for_zh: 棒球运动员，在美国职业棒球大联盟投打俱佳，屡获最有价值球员。

people.name: Sota Fujii
people.known_for: Shogi player who became the first to hold all eight major titles at once.
people.known_for_zh: 将棋棋士，首位同时囊括全部八大头衔的棋手。

people.name: Shimon Sakaguchi
people.known_for: Immunologist who discovered regulatory T cells; Nobel Prize 2025.
people.known_for_zh: 免疫学家，发现调节性T细胞，获2025年诺贝尔生理学或医学奖。

people.name: Susumu Kitagawa
people.known_for: Chemist who developed metal-organic frameworks; Nobel Prize 2025.
people.known_for_zh: 化学家，开发金属有机框架材料，获2025年诺贝尔化学奖。
